title: Autotune SLIs and per-workload cost budgets for console analytics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Console analytics ingestion and transformation workloads exhibit variable cost and latency patterns by tenant and by workload (batch vs realtime). Current SLOs are static and set at product-level, which leads to either over-provisioning (high cost) or missed alerts for tenant-level regressions. Goal: implement an adaptive SLO feedback loop that (1) creates per-workload SLIs with cost-awareness, (2) exposes a per-tenant cost budget signal, and (3) provides safe automated adjustments to alert thresholds and budgeting recommendations while keeping manual override and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument per-workload SLIs for ingestion, transform latency P50/P95/P99 and steady-state token processing rate
Surface per-tenant cost-budget signal (estimated token CPU/GPU cost) and show variance from baseline on dashboards
Deploy an SLO controller that suggests threshold adjustments via a feature-flagged canary and exposes 'recommend' vs 'apply' actions
Implement trace linkage from ingestion message ID through transformer jobs to dashboard traces for root-cause
Runbook updated with rollback steps and customer-facing incident messaging templates
notes: We will start with three canonical workloads: realtime-parse, batch-ingest, and embeddings-index. Each workload will have a distinct SLI shape and expected cost profile.

Controller design: compute recommended SLO deltas based on rolling baseline (30d), anomaly detection on error/latency using EWMA + robust MAD, then output suggestions scored by confidence and estimated cost delta.
Safety: any automated 'apply' path must be guarded by a per-tenant kill switch and a global rate limiter. Default deployment will be 'recommend-only' for 4 weeks across low-risk tenants.
We will coarsely bucket tenants into cost tiers (free, low, medium, enterprise) and only allow automated adjustments for low and medium tiers in the initial phase.

Trace linkage requires adding a persistent 'ingest_message_id' to the metadata propagated through the transformer pipeline and logged in both frontend span and backend worker spans. This will increase trace cardinality; we will couple with adaptive sampling.
decisions: Use rolling 30-day baseline for adaptivity rather than absolute global targets to respect workload seasonality.
Expose both 'recommend' and 'apply' actions; 'apply' gated behind entitlement and a feature flag.
Prioritize P95 latency and 99th token processing errors as primary SLIs for initial rollout.
Implement cost-estimation model using token counts * historical unit-cost per model variant; keep model simple for first iteration to avoid calibration drift.
tradeoffs: Adaptive SLOs reduce manual alert tuning but add complexity and risk of feedback loops — mitigated by canarying and recommend-only phase.
Per-tenant trace ids improve root-cause debugging but increase storage and cardinality costs; mitigate with adaptive sampling and TTL'd trace metadata.
Automatically applying SLO changes may obscure long-term regressions if controllers overfit short-lived anomalies — will require supervised thresholds and manual review for enterprise tier.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrument SLIs for canonical workloads + add ingest_message_id propagation (ENG telemetry changes)
Week 2: Implement cost-estimation signal and Grafana dashboards for tenant buckets
Week 3: Build SLO controller prototype (recommend-only) and wire to alerting UI
Week 4: Canary recommend-only across 10% of low/medium tenants, collect feedback
Week 5: If stable, enable 'apply' behind feature flag for low-tier with manual review logs
risks_and_mitigations: False positives in anomaly detection -> require minimum 3-sample confirmation and backoff before recommending change
Increased telemetry cost -> gate high-cardinality traces behind sampling and TTL on ingest_message_id retention
Customer confusion about automatic SLO changes -> surface audit log entries in console and enable tenant-level opt-out
